newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN DEBTOR TRACK RECORD WORSENS IN APRIL - CSS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN DEBTOR TRACK RECORD WORSENS IN APRIL - CSS.

text.p: The track record of South African debtors worsened in April with civil summonses for debt soaring a seasonally adjusted 62.7 percent from the previous month.
The Central Statistical Service (CSS) said civil cases and summonses against businesses and private persons totalled 172,098 in April from 105,768 in March and 111,220 a year ago.
For the three months to April a total of 389,641 summonses were issued from 342,267 previously.

The CSS said the three-month increase was due mainly to a 30.4 percent rise in debts related to non-professional services and a 22.1 percent rise in bad loans and a 16.8 percent rise in defaults on payments for goods sold on open account.
Civil judgments of debt cases in April involved a total of 428.2 million rand worth of debt, up from 342.2 million in March.
